title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Seasoning Relief on Entitlement Held Back after Liquidation
content:
On a VA Home Loan Guaranty loan liquidated by foreclosure, compromise sale or deed in lieu, the amount of entitlement held back against the unrecovered guaranty loss is reduced for seasoning according to how long before today the loan was liquidated. The liquidation date is the date the loan record shows the loan as closed by its liquidation; the time since is counted in months to today.

## Seasoning relief

| Loan liquidated | Reduction of the amount held back |
|---|---|
| At least 5 years (60 months) before today | 20 percent |
| At least 3 years (36 months) but less than 5 years before today | 10 percent |
| Otherwise (less than 3 years before today) | No reduction for seasoning (0 percent) |

A reduction of a percentage means the amount held back is multiplied by one minus that percentage divided by one hundred: 20 percent leaves 0.80 of it, 10 percent leaves 0.90 of it.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical liquidation dates, in months before today)

| Months since liquidation | Relief |
|---|---|
| 35 | 0 |
| 36 | 10 |
| 59 | 10 |
| 60 | 20 |
| 84 | 20 |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

A hypothetical amount held back of 15,000.00 dollars on a loan liquidated 62 months before today is reduced by 20 percent: 15,000.00 times one minus 20 divided by one hundred, or 12,000.00 dollars.
